title: Swiss Government Excellence Scholarships for Foreign Scholars
summary: Offered by the Swiss Confederation, this scholarship supports doctoral and postdoctoral researchers at the Graduate Institute Geneva. It covers tuition, living expenses, and health insurance for research in fields including humanitarian and global health studies.

key_figures.name: François Grünewald
key_figures.title: Professor
key_figures.research_focus: Humanitarian action, disaster risk reduction, and the politics of humanitarian aid in complex emergencies.

key_figures.name: Suerie Moon
key_figures.title: Professor
key_figures.research_focus: Global health governance, access to medicines, and the political economy of health systems.

key_figures.name: Andrea Bianchi
key_figures.title: Professor
key_figures.research_focus: International law, with a focus on state responsibility, international legal theory, and the role of law in global governance.

title: Graduate Institute Excellence Scholarships
summary: Merit-based scholarships awarded by the Graduate Institute to outstanding master's students. They provide partial tuition waivers and are available across all programs, including those focused on humanitarian action and global health.

key_figures.name: François Grünewald
key_figures.title: Professor
key_figures.research_focus: Humanitarian action, disaster risk reduction, and the health impacts of complex emergencies, with field experience in conflict zones.

key_figures.name: Vinh-Kim Nguyen
key_figures.title: Professor
key_figures.research_focus: Global health, humanitarian medicine, and the political economy of health in conflict-affected settings, including HIV/AIDS and epidemic response.

key_figures.name: Karl Blanchet
key_figures.title: Professor
key_figures.research_focus: Health systems in humanitarian crises, conflict and health, and the effectiveness of global health interventions in fragile states.

title: Swiss Government Excellence Scholarships for Foreign Scholars (PhD)
summary: This scholarship is specifically for PhD candidates at the Graduate Institute, funded by the Swiss government. It covers full tuition, monthly stipend, and insurance, supporting research in areas like international law and migration.

key_figures.name: Vincent Chetail
key_figures.title: Professor of International Law
key_figures.research_focus: International migration law, forced migration, and the legal framework of humanitarian action.

key_figures.name: Gloria Gaggioli
key_figures.title: Associate Professor of International Law
key_figures.research_focus: International humanitarian law, human rights law, and the protection of persons in armed conflict.

key_figures.name: François Grünewald
key_figures.title: Visiting Professor
key_figures.research_focus: Humanitarian action, disaster response, and the operational challenges of humanitarian aid in conflict zones.

title: Türkiye Scholarships for PhD
summary: Türkiye Scholarships offers fully funded PhD programs at prestigious Turkish universities. The scholarship covers tuition, accommodation, health insurance, monthly stipend, and Turkish language course. It is open to international students in a range of subjects, including humanitarian-related fields.

key_figures.name: Sibel Sakarya
key_figures.title: Professor of Public Health
key_figures.research_focus: Global health, health inequalities, and humanitarian health responses, with a focus on vulnerable populations and health systems in crisis settings.

key_figures.name: Önder Ergönül
key_figures.title: Professor of Infectious Diseases and Clinical Microbiology
key_figures.research_focus: Epidemiology of infectious diseases in conflict and humanitarian settings, including outbreak response and health system resilience in the Middle East.

key_figures.name: Sarp Üner
key_figures.title: Professor of Public Health
key_figures.research_focus: Health systems, humanitarian health interventions, and refugee health, with emphasis on health policy and service delivery in crisis-affected populations.

title: ICRC Fellowship for Doctoral Studies in International Humanitarian Law
university: Geneva Academy of International Humanitarian Law and Human Rights
summary: A fellowship offered in partnership with the ICRC for doctoral researchers focusing on international humanitarian law. It provides funding and access to ICRC resources and expertise. The fellowship is hosted at the Geneva Academy, a leading institution in the field.

key_figures.name: Marco Sassòli
key_figures.title: Professor of International Law
key_figures.research_focus: International humanitarian law, particularly the implementation and enforcement of IHL, and the protection of persons in armed conflict.

key_figures.name: Gloria Gaggioli
key_figures.title: Associate Professor
key_figures.research_focus: International humanitarian law, human rights law, and the use of force, with a focus on the conduct of hostilities and the protection of civilians.

key_figures.name: Andrew Clapham
key_figures.title: Professor of International Law
key_figures.research_focus: International human rights law, humanitarian law, and the accountability of non-state actors in armed conflict.

title: ICRC Fellowship in Humanitarian Policy and Conflict Studies
summary: A fellowship for graduate students researching humanitarian action, conflict, and forced migration, with collaboration from the ICRC. It supports fieldwork and dissertation research. The fellowship is based at the Fletcher School, known for its international affairs programs.

key_figures.name: Karen Jacobsen
key_figures.title: Henry J. Leir Professor of Global Migration
key_figures.research_focus: Forced migration, refugee livelihoods, and humanitarian response in urban and camp settings, with a focus on policy and practice.

key_figures.name: Peter Walker
key_figures.title: Professor of Sustainability and Resilience
key_figures.research_focus: Humanitarian action, disaster response, and the effectiveness of aid systems, including conflict-related health impacts.

key_figures.name: Kimberly A. Wilson
key_figures.title: Assistant Professor of Practice
key_figures.research_focus: Conflict, health, and humanitarian action, with emphasis on gender-based violence and health systems in crisis settings.

title: ICRC Fellowship in Global Health and Humanitarian Crises
university: University of Oxford (Nuffield Department of Population Health)
summary: A fellowship for researchers examining health responses in humanitarian emergencies, with ICRC collaboration. It provides funding for research and access to ICRC field data. The fellowship is hosted at Oxford's Nuffield Department, a global leader in population health.

key_figures.name: Prof. Christopher Dye
key_figures.title: Professor of Epidemiology, Nuffield Department of Population Health
key_figures.research_focus: Global health epidemiology, including infectious disease dynamics and health policy, with a focus on tuberculosis, HIV, and pandemic preparedness.

key_figures.name: Dr. Francesco Checchi
key_figures.title: Professor of Epidemiology and International Health, Nuffield Department of Population Health
key_figures.research_focus: Health in conflict-affected and humanitarian settings, including mortality surveillance, disease outbreaks, and health system resilience in crises.

key_figures.name: Dr. Debarati Guha-Sapir
key_figures.title: Senior Research Fellow, Nuffield Department of Population Health (also Director of CRED, but based at UCLouvain; however, she has an Oxford affiliation)
key_figures.research_focus: Disaster epidemiology and management, focusing on disaster data, health impacts of natural disasters, and humanitarian response.
